subject: maths

concepts.title: Optimisation Problem and Decision Variables
concepts.definition: An optimisation problem seeks to identify the best values for unknown decision variables to achieve maximum benefit or minimum expense under given limits.
concepts.key_idea: Representing choices as non-negative variables and goal metrics as a linear algebraic function.
question_patterns: define an optimisation problem in linear programming
identify the decision variables in a linear programming scenario
what constitutes an objective function and decision variables
explain non-negativity restrictions in formulation
Explain Optimisation Problem and Decision Variables with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Define non-negative quantities representing choices, such as x and y.
Express profit or cost as a linear expression Z = a*x + b*y to maximize or minimize.
Specify that all decision variables must satisfy x >= 0 and y >= 0 since quantities cannot be negative.

concepts.title: Linear Constraints and Feasible Region
concepts.definition: The region bounded by the simultaneous intersection of half-planes defined by all linear constraints and non-negativity conditions is called the feasible region.
concepts.key_idea: The intersection of half-planes forms a convex feasible region containing all viable solutions.
question_patterns: determine the feasible region for a given set of inequalities
verify if a given point is a feasible solution
distinguish between feasible and infeasible regions
check whether a coordinate satisfies all linear constraints
Explain Linear Constraints and Feasible Region with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Graph the boundary lines corresponding to linear inequalities on the Cartesian plane.
Shade the intersection of half-planes satisfying all inequalities along with x >= 0, y >= 0.

solution_steps.action: verify feasibility of a test point
solution_steps.explain: Substitute a candidate point into every constraint to confirm it lies within the feasible region.

concepts.title: Corner Point Method for Maximisation
concepts.definition: A graphic technique where the linear objective function is calculated at each corner point of a bounded feasible polygon to find its highest value.
concepts.key_idea: The extreme values of a linear function on a convex polygon always lie at its vertices.
question_patterns: find the maximum value of objective function using corner point method
calculate the optimal solution at vertices
solve the linear programming problem graphically for maximum profit
determine the optimal vertex for maximum Z
Numerical: apply Corner Point Method for Maximisation and compute the final value step by step.

worked_examples.question: Using Corner Point Method for Maximisation, compute the result for a = 3, x1 = 3, b = 3, y1 = 2, x2 = 2, y2 = 2, x3 = 1, y3 = 1, x4 = 1, y4 = 0.5.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: evaluate Z at first corner point: z1 = a * x1 + b * y1 = 15.0 Step 2: evaluate Z at second corner point: z2 = a * x2 + b * y2 = 12.0 Step 3: evaluate Z at third corner point: z3 = a * x3 + b * y3 = 6.0 Step 4: evaluate Z at fourth corner point: z4 = a * x4 + b * y4 = 4.5 Step 5: determine maximum value: z_max = max(z1, z2, z3, z4) = 15.0 Final result: 15.0

worked_examples.question: Using Corner Point Method for Maximisation, compute the result for a = 4, x1 = 4, b = 4, y1 = 3, x2 = 3, y2 = 3, x3 = 2, y3 = 2, x4 = 2, y4 = 1.5.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: evaluate Z at first corner point: z1 = a * x1 + b * y1 = 28.0 Step 2: evaluate Z at second corner point: z2 = a * x2 + b * y2 = 24.0 Step 3: evaluate Z at third corner point: z3 = a * x3 + b * y3 = 16.0 Step 4: evaluate Z at fourth corner point: z4 = a * x4 + b * y4 = 14.0 Step 5: determine maximum value: z_max = max(z1, z2, z3, z4) = 28.0 Final result: 28.0

concepts.title: Corner Point Method for Minimisation
concepts.definition: A method to compute the minimum value of a linear cost function by evaluating it at all corner points of the bounded feasible region.
concepts.key_idea: The smallest value of a linear objective function occurs at one of the vertices of the feasible polygon.
question_patterns: minimise the objective function graphically
find the minimum value of Z = ax + by
calculate the lowest cost from feasible corner points
determine optimal vertex for minimum Z
Numerical: apply Corner Point Method for Minimisation and compute the final value step by step.

solution_steps.explain: Calculate Z value at vertex (x2, y2)

solution_steps.explain: Calculate Z value at vertex (x3, y3)

worked_examples.solution: Step 1: evaluate Z at first corner point: z1 = a * x1 + b * y1 = 15.0 Step 2: evaluate Z at second corner point: z2 = a * x2 + b * y2 = 12.0 Step 3: evaluate Z at third corner point: z3 = a * x3 + b * y3 = 6.0 Step 4: determine minimum value: z_min = min(z1, z2, z3) = 6.0 Final result: 6.0

concepts.title: Multiple Optimal Solutions
concepts.definition: When two adjacent corner points yield the identical maximum or minimum value, every point on the line segment connecting them is also an optimal solution.
concepts.key_idea: Identical optimal values at two vertices imply infinite optimal solutions along their connecting boundary segment.
question_patterns: show that the linear programming problem has multiple optimal solutions
check if more than one vertex gives the same maximum value
explain why all points on a line segment give optimal Z
find conditions for multiple optimal solutions
Explain Multiple Optimal Solutions with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Calculate Z values for all vertices of the feasible region.
Identify if two distinct adjacent vertices yield the same optimal value M.
State that every point on the line segment connecting these two vertices produces the same optimal value M.

concepts.title: Unbounded Feasible Region and Optimality Test
concepts.definition: For an unbounded feasible region, candidate optimal values must be verified by checking whether the open half-plane ax + by > M (or < m) intersects the feasible region.
concepts.key_idea: An optimal value exists in an unbounded region only if the strict open half-plane has no points in common with the feasible region.
question_patterns: check if optimal value exists for an unbounded feasible region
test whether open half plane intersects feasible region
determine if an unbounded LPP has a maximum or minimum value
solve LPP with unbounded shaded region graphically
Explain Unbounded Feasible Region and Optimality Test with a suitable example.

solution_steps.action: find candidate optimal value m or M at vertices
solution_steps.explain: Calculate objective function values at corner points of the unbounded region.
Form the open inequality ax + by < m (for minimum) or ax + by > M (for maximum).
If the open half-plane shares common points with the feasible region, no optimal value exists; otherwise, m or M is optimal.

concepts.title: Infeasible Constraints and Non-Existence of Solution
concepts.definition: When a set of linear inequality constraints cannot be satisfied simultaneously by any point, no feasible region exists and the problem has no solution.
concepts.key_idea: Incompatible system of linear inequalities leads to an empty feasible set and no solution.
question_patterns: show that LPP has no feasible solution
determine if constraints are mutually contradictory
check why no shaded feasible region exists
explain non-existence of solution in linear programming
Explain Infeasible Constraints and Non-Existence of Solution with a suitable example.

solution_steps.explain: Plot each inequality on the coordinate plane including non-negativity axes.

solution_steps.action: verify absence of common shaded area
solution_steps.explain: Observe that there is no region satisfying all inequalities at once, concluding no feasible solution exists.
State that since the feasible region is empty, the linear programming problem has no solution.
